transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because after everyone goes to bed, I’ll start with some leftovers and then it just turns into a lot. Like, I’ve eaten half a tray of catered pasta, dessert from a client dinner, and whatever snacks are in the pantry all in one sitting.
When this happens, do you feel like you can’t stop eating or control how much you’re eating?

Yes. Once I start—especially after a tense night with my husband—it’s like the part of me that makes decisions just goes offline. I keep reaching for more even while I’m telling myself, “Patricia, stop. This is enough.”
After these episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit to try to undo the eating?
No, I don’t make myself vomit afterward.
After these eating episodes, do you do anything to try to make up for them, like taking laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?
I’m not really sure what counts as making up for it. I usually just feel bad afterward, but I don’t know.
After one of these eating episodes, do you intentionally skip meals or go without eating to try to make up for it?
I’m not sure. I mean, I feel guilty afterward, but I haven’t really noticed myself deliberately skipping meals because of it.
After these eating episodes, do you exercise on purpose to burn off the calories?
I don’t think I do that on purpose, no. I might exercise normally, but not specifically to burn off what I ate.
After one of these eating episodes, do you intentionally go a long time without eating to make up for it?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself intentionally going a long time without eating afterward.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress?

Yes, a lot. Afterward I feel embarrassed and disgusted with myself, like I’ve ruined this disciplined person I’m supposed to be. I just sit there thinking I should’ve gone for a run or done yoga instead.
After these episodes, do you ever use laxatives, diuretics, or diet pills to try to undo the eating?
No, I haven’t used anything like that after an episode.
When this happens, are you eating an unusually large amount of food within a short period of time?
Yes. I’ll start with leftovers after everyone’s asleep, and then I end up eating half a tray of pasta, dessert from a client dinner, and whatever snacks are in the pantry—all in one sitting.
How often do these eating episodes happen?
For the last three months, it’s been at least one night almost every week. Usually after an argument or a late work event, and some weeks it happens twice.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent binge-eating episodes characterized by consuming an objectively large amount of food in one sitting with a clear sense of loss of control, occurring about weekly for the last 3 months, with marked distress. She denied self-induced vomiting and denied intentional compensatory behaviors such as excessive exercise, prolonged fasting, or use of laxatives/diuretics/diet pills. This is most consistent with binge-eating disorder, coded in ICD-10 under other eating disorders.
